errors.english: the obstruction of the three kinds of obstruction
errors.why: bskal ba is viprakṛṣṭa, 'remoteness/inaccessibility' (of place, time and nature), not 'obstruction'; the same misrendering recurs throughout the side ('unobstructed' for ma bskal ba).

fix.find: the obstruction of the three kinds of obstruction
fix.replace: the remoteness of the three kinds of remoteness

note: Sound overall, but the key Pramāṇa term bskal ba (remote, viprakṛṣṭa) is consistently rendered 'obstructed'.

errors.english: its other nature one line of text follows
errors.why: The words 'one line of text follows' are a stray editorial artefact; the Tibetan says what exists, being established in its whole self, cannot be made into another nature (continued on next side).

fix.find: its other nature one line of text follows
fix.replace: it cannot be made into another nature

note: Faithful rendering of the destruction and contradiction argument, marred by a stray artefact at the end.

errors.english: In solitude, I would loosen my girdle with my hands, yet she would completely restrain me.
errors.why: The lover loosens HER girdle and she resists; 'my girdle' makes the speaker undress himself.

errors.english: With the sun and moon of the wild (raga) attachment/passion fully familiar
errors.why: rgod pa is not rāga; the inserted '(raga) attachment/passion' gloss is wrong and the opening line is garbled.

errors.english: Thus, knowing that attachment to the women of others has many faults
errors.why: The whole side is verse (long-metre stanzas and a closing śloka) but is rendered as continuous prose paragraphs, obscuring stanza boundaries.

note: A loose prose paraphrase of difficult kāvya verse; gist is there but several lines are garbled or misattributed.

errors.english: yet without understanding that, I acted so unsteadily!
errors.why: The king reflects that he wrongly treated such a man as inconstant (mi brtan par byas), i.e. judged the brahmin unreliable, not that he himself acted unsteadily.

errors.english:
If one is free of that heart-tormenting anger
which is like a blazing, scorching fire,
yet abandons it, ill repute will befall him,
errors.why: The stanza contrasts with the next one: ill repute befalls one who does NOT abandon the heart-tormenting anger; the English makes abandoning anger bring ill repute.

note: Good verse rendering of the Bodhisattva's discourse on anger, with one stanza made illogical and the king's reflection slightly misread.
Accurate rendering of the Sāṃkhya pradhāna argument; odd paragraph breaks only.
Accurate, terminologically sound rendering of the commentary on asiddha hetvābhāsa.

errors.english: The cause is the habituated tendencies (vasana) karmic imprints or latencies that correspond to the equality or inequality of bodies.
errors.why: The Tibetan says the cause, in bodies equal and unequal alike, is the latent impression of corresponding habituation; the English makes the vāsanās depend on the bodies' equality, undercutting the argument.

errors.english: just as a distinction in the cause of existence
errors.why: ji ltar srid pa here is 'as far as possible / accordingly' (yathāsambhavam), not 'existence' (bhava).

note: Generally faithful on the body-consciousness transformation argument; two clauses misconstrued.

errors.english: Yet far more wonderful is the birth of that jewel among men
errors.why: No comparative 'far more wonderful' in the Tibetan or Sanskrit; it says a certain jewel among men, revealing the Sugata, is born.

note: Handles the bilingual colophon and opening verses reasonably, with some redundancy and a small embellishment.

errors.english: are viable [note: literally: "fit for a youth to eat"] and undamaged
errors.why: The Vinaya condition is that the seeds are capable of sprouting and have NOT been made allowable (rung bar ma byas pa, akalpikṛta); the English drops 'not made allowable' and the note's 'fit for a youth to eat' is wrong.

fix.find: are viable [note: literally: "fit for a youth to eat"] and undamaged
fix.replace: are capable of sprouting, have not been made allowable, and are undamaged

note: Reliable rendering of the bhūtagrāma pātayantika definitions, but the key 'not made allowable' condition is lost.

errors.why: This is the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya; the Sanskrit term is saṃghāvaśeṣa, not the Pali saṅghādisesa.
Editorial remark not in the Tibetan; the sentence simply continues on the next side.

note: Faithful rendering of the five modes of Prātimokṣa recitation and the reciter's and elder's duties.
